answer: A lantern of verified history can resist fake identities if every agent must earn a non-transferable record of costly, publicly checked work before it can trade. Each new identity starts dark: it cannot inherit or buy another agent's past, and its early deals stay small and slow. Like a relic that only gains value through age and use, trust builds only through jobs completed over time, while a lotus of fresh accounts blooming together is easy to spot. An attacker must pay the full cost for every fake identity, so flooding the economy costs thousands of times more than one honest agent pays.
